name: AtomStack A70 Max
tagline: 70–77W CoS-packaged diode: 850×800 mm flagship Atomstack cutter
tldr: AtomStack A70 Max brings 70–77W compressed diode power to an 850×800 mm frame with auto-focus, touchscreen, and claims of 25 mm wood in one pass. Popular 2024–2025 upgrade path for makers outgrowing A40 Pro: still open-frame, not enclosed.
mainObjective: Maximum Atomstack diode power for large panels and deep wood cuts

priceRange.note: Official Atomstack store, Oct 2026: $1,639 to $3,029 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Strongest cut headroom in the line: about 28 mm basswood-class stock in benchmarks
One button switches the same head between 70W for cutting and 35W for finer engraving: no module to swap
Large 850 × 800 mm bed with one-key auto-focus, touchscreen controller and built-in air assist
cons: Clear cast acrylic and thick production cutting still favor CO₂, not diode power alone
Confirm optical wattage on the listing before you buy
beginnerNotes: The frame takes about 1056 × 1168 mm of table, more than the work area suggests: measure your bench first. Open frame: wear the supplied glasses, add exhaust, and run your first engraving tests in 35W mode.
proTips: Cut in 70W mode; engrave photos in 35W mode, which has the smaller spot (0.08 × 0.12 mm against 0.12 × 0.18 mm). Atomstack's thickest one-pass cuts are best-case figures: quote customers from your own scrap tests.
primaryUse: Large-format high-power diode for production-style wood and acrylic cutting plus detailed engraving.

editorialDepth.advantages: AtomStack A70 Max 70W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: How big is the AtomStack A70 Max?
faq.answer: 850 × 800 mm of work area in a frame of about 1056 × 1168 × 230 mm, per Atomstack's spec sheet. Atomstack also sells it with an enclosure ($2,329 bundle in November 2026).

faq.question: Is the A70 Max 70W or 35W?
faq.answer: Both, from one head switched with a button: 70W (rated 70–77W) for cutting, 35W (35–39W) with a smaller spot for detailed engraving.

faq.question: How thick can the A70 Max cut?
faq.answer: Atomstack claims about 25 mm of wood in one pass and 26 mm of dark acrylic. Treat those as best-case figures; our benchmark cuts 3–6 mm wood at 10–20 mm/s. Clear acrylic stays out of reach, as with any blue diode.

faq.question: How much does the A70 Max cost?
faq.answer: On Atomstack's US store in November 2026: $1,519 machine only during the holiday sale (usually $1,639 with the Basic Bundle), $1,839 for the Pro Bundle and $2,329 for the Enclosure Bundle.

faq.question: A70 Max or Sculpfun S70 Max?
faq.answer: Same 70W diode class and a similar bed (830 × 800 mm on the Sculpfun). The A70 Max adds the 35W engraving mode, auto-focus and a touchscreen; compare current prices, as both brands run frequent promotions.
